task: Accept an optional user_context field on /bridge and forward it to downstream MCP tools as _meta under codemie.ai/user-context on tools/call only, with defensive PII masking in service logs.

key_reasoning.reason: Six source components across three layers plus a shared utility: models/request.py (BridgeRequestBody), server/routes.py (bridge_endpoint and both mode handlers), client/manager.py (invoke_with_timeout), client/single_usage.py (execute_single_usage_request plus three transport helpers), client/methods.py (invoke_mcp_method tools/call branch), and utils/masking.py (new mask_user_context). Scope is bounded rather than XL because the analysis confirmed managed.py/ManagedClient has no parallel invocation path, and generate_cache_key, apply_substitutions and extract_request_context are explicit field allowlists so the new field is inert in all three by construction.

The closest existing pattern is utils/masking.py's flat dict[str, str] maskers plus the private _mask_params_recursive in methods.py; neither covers the security-sensitive aspect of this work — recursive traversal of an opaque nested dict with per-key policy and partial redaction of username, with SENSITIVE_PATTERNS explicitly off-limits for widening. That is a divergence from precedent on a PII-exposure path, so Technical Risk was raised. Compounding it: the DEBUG_LOG_BRIDGE_PAYLOAD block (routes.py:276-283) is the untested, opt-in-by-env place a new top-level field leaks in the clear; the mcp 1.30.0 call_tool meta kwarg could not be verified on disk; and mypy --strict is the only gate with no CI behind it. Not scored XXL because the change is fully reversible — field absent means no meta passed and byte-identical behaviour.

Roughly 8-12 modified files, 0-1 new: six source files, README.md, tests/conftest.py (its fixed four-positional single_usage_side_effect sits on a changed signature), plus edits to test_mcp_methods.py, test_masking.py, test_bridge_validation.py and a first-of-its-kind negative cache-key test. Sits at the L/XL boundary on modified count but lands at L because new files are 0-1, far below XL's 4-6.

red_flags_applied: Technical Risk bumped from L to XL: PII handling and log-exposure prevention are a primary requirement (defensive masking of an opaque user_context, untested DEBUG_LOG_BRIDGE_PAYLOAD dump path).

Sanitization red flag checked: no existing reusable masking util is adequate for the nested/partial-redaction surface. Technical Risk floor of L already exceeded by the applied bump, so no further increase.

Edge-case test-template gap noted (no precedent for a negative cache-key test, no nested/partial masking test block, no direct route-handler tests). Recorded as part of the same Technical Risk divergence rather than a second additive bump, since it stems from the identical missing-precedent signal.
